rounds.text: Sky Gold & Diamonds Ltd exhibits extraordinary top-line and bottom-line expansion, with a 3-year compounded sales growth of 76% and profit growth of 144% [E14, E16]. This aggressive momentum is paired with elite profitability metrics, including a 3-year median return on equity of 27% and an ROCE of 26.67%, both of which vastly outperform their sector benchmarks of 8.89% and 10.28% [E9, E10, E22]. Operating efficiency is further reinforced by a structurally increasing yearly operating-margin trend over the last seven years, alongside gross margin expansion driven by high-demand product segments like uncut diamond jewelry [E26, E76, E80]. Strategic scalability is evident as the business surpassed its original FY27 revenue target of ₹5,000 crore a year early while maintaining long-term aspirations of reaching ₹18,000 crores to ₹19,000 crores by FY30 [E72, E73]. Conceded: the stock trades at a rich valuation of 33.8x P/E with a high price-to-book ratio of 9.64x, and generated negative operating cash flow of ₹45 Cr for March 2026 [E1, E2, E29]. Institutional confidence remains robust, evidenced by positive money flow and a sharp increase in domestic and foreign institutional holdings since December 2023 [E36, E37, E38].

Sky Gold & Diamonds Ltd currently trades at a significant premium, with a price-to-book ratio of 9.64x compared to a sector benchmark of 2x [E2, E7]. This valuation is further strained by the fact that the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00%, offering no immediate cash return to shareholders despite its reported profitability [E4, E56]. While the company has shown rapid growth, the market price has outpaced profit growth by 32%, suggesting that investor expectations may be running ahead of actual delivery [E51]. Furthermore, the company reported a negative operating cash flow of Rs -45 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -140 Cr in March 2026, raising questions about the quality of its earnings [E29, E30]. The risk profile is compounded by a notable reduction in promoter holdings, which have decreased by 10.34 percentage points since December 2023 [E35]. Conceded: The company has demonstrated strong compounded sales and profit growth [E14, E16], and management has successfully surpassed its original FY27 revenue target a year early [E72].

While the bear highlights a premium price-to-book ratio of 9.64x against a sector benchmark of 2x [E2, E7], this valuation is fully justified by elite operational returns, including an ROE of 28.17% and ROCE of 26.67% that dwarf sector benchmarks of 8.89% and 10.28% [E8, E9, E10]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], but this capital is actively deployed to fuel exceptional 3-year compounded sales growth of 76% and profit growth of 144% [E14, E16]. Regarding concerns that price has outpaced profit growth by 32% [E51], that lag is neutralized by stellar institutional accumulation, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings surging and generating positive money flow [E36, E37, E38]. Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -45 Cr in March 2026 [E29], but H1 FY27 operating cash flow aggressively rebounded to INR 136 crores [E86], while the net working capital cycle compressed to 55 days [E88]. Finally, the reduction in promoter holding [E35] is met with a rigorous governance framework where promoters draw zero salary starting in FY27, tying their compensation strictly to operating cash flow dividends [E94].

Conceded: H1 FY27 operating cash flow rebounded to INR 136 crores [E86]. However, the bull's reliance on high ROE (28.17%) and ROCE (26.67%) to justify a 9.64x P/B multiple ignores the stark reality of severe structural cash generation deficits and historical volatility [E2, E8, E9, E10, E48]. The bull attributes the negative cash flow of Rs -45 Cr in March 2026 [E29] to a temporary blip, yet total borrowings simultaneously climbed to Rs 964 Cr by September 2026 [E33]. While the bull points to surging institutional accumulation [E36, E37, E38], this does not negate the fact that insider confidence has dropped significantly as promoter holdings fell by 10.34 percentage points down to 51.74% [E35]. Furthermore, dismissing the 32% gap where price growth outpaced profit growth [E51] glosses over the underlying risk of earnings growth decelerating [E63]. Finally, the governance framework of zero promoter salary tied to operating cash flow [E94] arrives on the heels of an exceptional charge of INR 7.35 crores for a fraud incident at subsidiary Star Mangalsutra [E89], rendering executive pledges a reactive fix rather than a proven safety buffer.

Conceded: promoter holding fell to 51.74% [E35], and the company recorded an exceptional charge of INR 7.35 crores for a fraud incident [E89]. However, the bear's claim of structural cash deficits ignores the verified rebound to INR 136 crores of operating cash flow in H1 FY27 [E86], directly invalidating the backward-looking read on annual figures. The rise in borrowings to INR 964 crores [E33] accompanies massive operational expansion, evidenced by the original FY27 revenue target of ₹5,000 crore being surpassed a year early [E72]. The bear's worry over decelerating earnings growth [E63] is neutralized by Q2 FY27 gross profits surging 87% to INR 229 crores [E80] and an institutional money flow reading of positive money flow [E38] backed by domestic institutions scaling up to 12.44% [E37]. Furthermore, the transition of promoter remuneration to depend strictly on operating cash flows [E94] establishes robust shareholder alignment rather than a mere reactive fix.

Conceded: H1 FY27 operating cash flow reached INR 136 crores [E86]. However, the bull's dismissal of annual cash generation ignores that as of Mar 2026, annual operating cash flow stood at a negative Rs -45 Cr alongside a severe free cash flow deficit of Rs -140 Cr [E29, E30]. The bull points to the early achievement of revenue targets [E72] to justify rising debt, but total borrowings actually expanded to Rs 964 Cr by Sep 2026 [E33], while the screen explicitly flags earnings growth as decelerating [E63]. Furthermore, citing institutional accumulation [E37] sidesteps the primary governance red flag: promoter holding has secularly dropped by 10.34 percentage points to 51.74% [E35], down 21.8% over three years [E57]. Finally, while the bull praises executive alignment via tied promoter remuneration [E94], this noble gesture follows a literal fraud incident at subsidiary Star Mangalsutra that required a INR 7.35 crore exceptional charge [E89].
